summary.en: Salvadoran forces of about 2,000 are searching for four soldiers missing after a gang ambush near Port-au-Prince while denying airstrikes. Haitian gang leaders have written to the United Nations seeking mediation, with one leader saying he has raised the white flag and warning President Bukele about rising violence. The UN chief condemned a recent attack in Haiti that killed 47 people. The United Nations confirmed 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker på rundt 2 000 leter etter fire soldater som er savnet etter et gjengoverfall i nærheten av Port-au-Prince, samtidig som de benekter luftangrep. Haitiske gjengledere har skrevet til FN og ber om mekling, og en leder sier at han har heist det hvite flagget og advarer president Bukele om økende vold. FN-sjefen fordømte et nylig angrep i Haiti som drepte 47 personer. FN bekreftet 193 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
